text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ste. Agathe falls, Winnipeg wary: Wind drives flood water into town, raising fears of what Red River crest will do to city.
- Morin forensic evidence tainted: Witness reveals laboratory foul-up.
- Reform spills new red book: Liberals are livid over leak of text.
- Under seige/ Development is destroying one of Zimbabwe's natural wonders: Where wild things increasingly aren't.
- Vaccine keeps apes HIV-free for a year: Resistance found to massive viral dose.
- Markets take flight: U.S. Canadian stocks and bonds rally as low-inflation figures suggest interest rate calm.
- Andrew Sarlos dies of heart failure: Buddha of Bay Street helped shape Corporate Canada.
- Petrocan, partners broaden East Coast oil ambitions: Plan subsea pipelines network to help extract new reserves.
- Jim Bob in control at Freeport meeting.
- Liberals head for a landslide victory: poll.
- Freeport holds firm: Further testing of samples from holes covering thousands of acres of Busang still shows no gold, says Jim Bob Moffett.
- Markets ditch inflation fears and soar.
